claim: Contract resolution rules can permit an exceptional non-binary payout (an Unknown/50-50 redemption at 0.50 per token) in addition to disputes and post-launch clarifications, so a schema cannot assume every settlement is a clean binary 0/1.
locator: Resolution Rules; UMA Vote table; Clarifications
limitations: Documents one venue's mechanism as of the inspection date; not a claim that every venue or contract shares this exact exceptional payout or frequency.

claim: An event container grouping multiple markets does not by itself establish that the grouped outcome tokens are mutually exclusive or form an exhaustive partition.
limitations: Actual contract compatibility for a specific event still requires reading that event's own rules; this is not a claim about any particular event's structure.

claim: Live and historical partitions for a venue's records are governed by moving cutoffs with object-specific partition fields, and the documented historical endpoints do not establish a complete historical order-book archive.
limitations: Describes one venue's documented interface as of the inspection date; does not establish coverage completeness, redistribution permission, or behavior of any other venue.

claim: The selected real-data study period (January 1975-December 2025) deliberately excludes the March 1958-April 1974 window that the source header attributes to Scripps Institution of Oceanography, and separately excludes interpolation-flagged months and treats the December 2022-July 2023 Maunakea substitution as a location discontinuity.
locator: Header attribution; interpolation/negative-flag fields; Maunakea substitution note
limitations: A provenance and scope boundary for one dataset, not a claim about data quality elsewhere in the series or about any market or forecasting application.

claim: Retrieved terms-of-use text did not expose complete operative permissions, so no unrestricted venue-data redistribution license was established for the inspected venue documentation.
limitations: A partial-response boundary, not a legal determination about any reader's eligibility or about redistribution rights for any other page or venue.

claim: A provider's own documentation states that later quality-control checks can revise previously published monthly values, so a current-vintage download does not reconstruct a historical vintage.
limitations: States that revisions can occur in principle; this book has not measured any specific NOAA revision magnitude, and the chapter's illustrative revision numbers are explicitly invented for exposition.

claim: Live/historical partitions use moving cutoffs with different fields governing different record types (for example, settlement versus trade-creation partition times), so a single query surface cannot be assumed to hold every past record.
limitations: Documents one venue's interface design as of the inspection date; general pagination/cutoff engineering practice described in the chapter is stated independent of any single provider's exact field names.

claim: The inspected order-book schema uses string-valued fixed-point dollar prices and quantities in YES/NO bid arrays, with an ordinary binary contract's opposite-side bid implying an ask.
limitations: Describes one documented response schema as of the inspection date; a current schema example is not historical order-book evidence and may change.

claim: The inspected public CLOB documentation returns price/size levels alongside a book timestamp, a state hash, a minimum order size, and a tick size for a given token.
limitations: A state hash identifies one returned snapshot; it does not establish complete historical coverage or queue-position information.

claim: Documented resolution can include a challenge/dispute period after an initial proposed outcome, so the economically informative outcome can become knowable before funds are finally settled.
limitations: Describes one venue's documented process; indicative timelines are not guarantees of payout timing for any specific contract.

claim: White's inspected construction compares a candidate-family maximum with a benchmark and uses dependent common-block resampling under stationary strong-mixing assumptions.
limitations: Inspection depth follows the source audit; not all Appendix assumptions or proofs were read. No repair for undisclosed search, leakage or incorrect execution.

claim: Reading pointer for the false-discovery-rate objective and a stated control result under an independence-based testing setup.
limitations: Do not assume arbitrary-dependence validity for the original procedure from this abstract-level record; a defined testing family and valid p-values remain necessary.

claim: The inspected institutional abstract proposes a probability-of-backtest-overfitting framework and a combinatorially symmetric cross-validation method, and warns that repeated holdout inspection undermines the validity of a supposedly held-out evaluation.
limitations: CSCV is not presented here as a universal cure for dependent event labels; the warning about repeated inspection is used to motivate this chapter's own frozen-confirmatory-design argument, not as a certified numeric threshold.

claim: The inspected Gneiting-Raftery sections define propriety and present categorical quadratic and logarithmic scores.
limitations: The chapter independently derives its binary losses; the source uses rewards and a two-outcome quadratic sum. Not every proof or application was inspected.

claim: Reading pointer identifying the historical origin of the quadratic (Brier) probability-verification score.
limitations: Bibliographic identity only; this book's single-YES normalization is defined independently and is not claimed to match the original paper's exact convention.

claim: Reading pointer for probability-score decomposition; population identities must be distinguished from binned estimates.
limitations: Bibliographic identity only; the reliability-resolution-uncertainty identity and the worked binned-estimate counterexample in this chapter are derived and numerically verified independently, not taken from the original text.

claim: The inspected abstract reports miscalibration in studied modern neural classifiers and reports that temperature scaling was effective on most examined datasets.
limitations: Image/document classifier experiments; does not establish calibration behavior on small, shifting event-market samples.

claim: The inspected abstract reports that isotonic calibration can overfit small samples and that logistic calibration can sometimes worsen probabilities, motivating a proposed beta-calibration method.
limitations: Classifier-specific comparisons in the original paper do not establish a universally best calibration method; this book has not implemented beta calibration.

claim: The inspected calibration sections distinguish base fitting from calibration data and report model- and sample-dependent calibration benefits and harms.
locator: Author PDF pp. 1-3 and 8; methods and conclusions
limitations: Random-sample benchmark results are not chronological event-market validation or a universal method ranking; inspection scope is the source audit's named sections.

claim: An equilibrium market price can, under stated sufficient conditions, reflect an average belief about an event's probability, with biased approximations discussed outside those conditions.
limitations: Working-paper abstract only; average belief is not objective event probability, and this is not a claim that any specific market price equals the true probability of any specific event.

claim: The inspected stationary-bootstrap abstract describes geometric random block lengths for weakly dependent stationary observations.
limitations: Original full proofs and an appropriate event-data block length were not inspected; the chapter's design-effect calculation is an independent classroom derivation.

claim: The inspected abstract and Section 2 text describe a time-uniform, nonparametric confidence-sequence construction with simultaneous-in-time coverage under a stated exponential-supermartingale/filtration setup.
locator: Inspected abstract and Section 2 (author HTML v9)
limitations: Time-uniform coverage is conditional on the paper's stated assumptions; it does not by itself cure event-group leakage or convert dependent repeated observations into independent ones.
